stories.headline: Kiwis gun reveals key to Ponga miracle
stories.summary: Superstar fullback Kayln Ponga has the captain's run to prove his fitness and make a miraculous return from a broken arm to play in NZ's World Cup semi-final.
stories.body:
Jahrome Hughes had a blinder for Melbourne 22 days after breaking his arm last year and says Kalyn Ponga is on track to make his own stunning comeback for New Zealand, if he can tick one key box.

Ponga, named on an extended bench for the Kiwis in Saturday night's semi-final at Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, trained strongly on Wednesday.

Coach Stacey Jones said Ponga had "a few boxes to tick" as he leant on the advice of Hughes.

Ponga played for more than 20 minutes with his injury in New Zealand's epic tournament-opening 24-22 loss to Australia, before undergoing surgery in the hope of returning for the finals.

Kiwis halfback Hughes broke his arm against Brisbane in a final-round game in 2025, before returning for the preliminary final to inspire a victory over Cronulla.

He said there was "one thing I told KP" that would be vital for Ponga to get back for the clash with red-hot Tonga, just 23 days after his own fracture..

"(Storm) had a week off after we won that first final, and we had a full opposed session and I wanted to get a full contact session in," Hughes said.

"That gave me all the confidence in the world that a week later I'd be able to do my job on the field. If I wasn't able to do that I wouldn't have played.

"(Ponga) has got to have confidence in his arm and feel right. You don't want him to worry about his arm the whole game because that will take away from his game.

"He is training really well. That's another step towards playing."

Jones kept his cards close to his chest when asked if Ponga would start the match if fit.

"We will get through one more session and see where it goes. Kalyn is looking pretty good," he said.

Ponga and fellow Newcastle fan favourite Phoenix Crossland, also named on an extended bench, could spell double trouble for Tonga.

A month after playing together in Newcastle's 19-18 NRL grand final loss to the Sydney Roosters, centre Dane Gagai is backing the former Dally M Medallist to terrorise Tonga, in what would be a huge boost for the Kiwis.

"That'll just come down to the boxes he'll have to tick with the physios and stuff, but one thing that's never in question is Kalyn's toughness and I don't think he gets enough credit or praise for it," Gagai said.

"Some of the games he's played with injury. It was only maybe a year or two ago with his AC (acromioclavicular joint) and getting that injected, but he'll put his head in most places that people won't put their hands.

"So I've got no doubt he'll do everything he can to make sure he can take that field. It's just a case of whether he can tick those boxes and he'll know whether he's capable of playing or not.

"He won't put himself before the team, but we'd obviously love to have him out there."

Jones said Crossland could also be a late inclusion, after completing a four-game suspension for a hip-drop tackle that broke Nathan Cleary's ankle in Newcastle's preliminary final victory over Penrith.

Knowing New Zealand will need their strongest possible line-up to keep Tonga at bay, Gagai also welcomed the prospect of the classy hooker featuring in the do-or-die showdown.

"He's come in a bit later into camp, but even though he wasn't playing he's always himself and brings a lot of energy," Gagai said.

"He's awesome to have around the place. It's going to be good to be able to chuck this jersey on with him and nice to know that the game against Penrith wasn't our last together.

"So I'm definitely looking forward to that and I'm super happy for him."

stories.headline: Fantasy buzz: Sit Henry? Start Dulcich? Matchup tips for 'TNF' and Week 9
stories.summary: With Baltimore's offense in disarray, should you bench Derrick Henry against Jacksonville on Thursday night?
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 5: Sit Derrick Henry on Thursday night?

By Michael F. Florio

Henry and the Baltimore Ravens play on Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It may sound bold, but fantasy managers should try and get away from "King Henry "if possible.

Henry has averaged just 8.6 fantasy PPG over the past three weeks. His yards per carry drops from 4.2 in Weeks 1-4 (with Lamar Jackson) to 3.7 in Weeks 5-8 (without Jackson). His explosive run rate, yards before and after contact per carry also drop without Jackson.

Now he faces the Jaguars, who have allowed a league-low 58 rushing yards per game to RBs. They've allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs and rate well metrically against the run. Their one weakness is pass catching backs, but Henry averages fewer than two targets per game.

Those in deeper leagues likely do not have a choice but to start him and hope for the best. However, if you have the capability to sit him, I would. Some options I like over him are Jonah Coleman, Chase Brown, Ashton Jeanty, Quinshon Judkins, Cam Skattebo, Rhamondre Stevenson, Breece Hall and Blake Corum.

More matchup tips to know

Jordan Love has been airing the ball out more. In his last four games, he has averaged seven deep pass attempts per game, up from 4.5 in the first four games. That's led from fantasy PPG jumping from 16.2 to 21. Now he gets the New England Patriots, who have allowed a 42% completion percentage on deep passes, well above league average of 36%.
Dak Prescott averages just 4.0 yards per attempt and 44.8% completion rate when under pressure. From a clean pocket he averages 7.9 YPA and 73.5% completion rate. He faces the Indianapolis Colts, who generate pressure at a league-low 27%, the next closest is 31%.
Malik Willis has averaged 19.8 fantasy PPG in his last three games. He has thrown multiple passing TDs in two straight games. He gets the Detroit Lions this week who have allowed the most pass yards per game, fantasy PPG and pass TDs this season. He is the top streaming option for those who lost Jackson.
Jeanty has been most effective as a receiver. This week he gets the San Francisco 49ers who have allowed the most catches to RBs and the fifth-most receiving yards. In fact, 92% of passes throw to RBs against them have been completed, the second-highest in the NFL.
Coleman is tied with James Cook III for third-highest explosive run rate among RBs. He leads the Denver Broncos backs in that, missed tackles forced rate, yards after contact per carry and yards per route ran. He faces the Carolina Panthers, who are second in the NFL in rushing TDs and fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
Skattebo faces the Philadelphia Eagles who have allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs. In fact, RB1s have averaged 18.2 fantasy PPG against them over the past three weeks.
Luther Burden III has averaged 19.9 fantasy PPG since Caleb Williams returned. Only five receivers average that number or higher this season. He leads the Chicago Bears with a 21% target share against zone coverage, which the Tampa Bay Buccaneers play 82% of the time. Burden has picked up 52% of his receiving yards after the catch and Tampa Bay has allowed the second-most YAC in the NFL.
Parker Washington plays 41% of his snaps from the slot and the Ravens have allowed the most touchdowns and eighth-most yards to players in the slot. They have allowed the third-most yards to receivers this season. Washington is worth sticking with on Thursday night.
Malik Washington is a strong streaming option this week. He has scored 11-plus fantasy points in four of his last five games. He also leads the Miami Dolphins with a 43% slot snap share. The Lions have allowed the most yards and touchdowns to players in the slot. They have allowed the fourth-most fantasy PPG to WRs.
Greg Dulcich is another Dolphin worth streaming this week! He is second in Miami in slot snaps (41%) and as it says above, that matters this week. Plus, the Lions have allowed the most touchdowns and fantasy PPG to tight ends.
Harold Fannin Jr averaged 14.9 fantasy PPG with Shedeur Sanders last year, that was 9.9 with all other QBs. He's had nine-plus targets in his each of last two games and went for 245 yards in those. Fannin remains a strong start regardless of who the Cleveland Browns' QB is this week.

Nov. 4: Garrett Wilson's concussion could create more opportunities for Jets playmakers

By Eric Moody

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced Wednesday that Wilson is in the concussion protocol. Wilson played the entire game against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, finishing with six catches for 83 yards on 12 targets. If cleared, I'd still start Wilson as a low-end WR2, even though the Chiefs have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

If Wilson cannot play, Adonai Mitchell is the first receiver I'd look to add. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown last week, finishing with 27.2 fantasy points. I'd view Mitchell as an upside WR4.

Omar Cooper Jr. could also see more targets, but I'd leave him on the bench. He had consecutive 100-yard games before going without a target against the Raiders.

Mason Taylor is worth considering if you need help at tight end. He's drawn at least five targets in three consecutive games and faces a Chiefs defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to the position.

Have a plan in the event of a Jonathan Taylor trade
Jonathan Taylor has been mentioned in trade rumors, and there's a chance the Indianapolis Colts move him before Sunday. Managers who roster Taylor should add Seth McGowan (rostered in 21.6% of ESPN leagues) as insurance. If Taylor is traded (or made a Sunday inactive while the team continues to work on a deal), McGowan could see a much larger workload against a Cowboys defense that's allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to running backs.

Nov. 4: Bhayshul Tuten questionable for Thursday night
By Michael DiRocco, NFL Nation Jaguars reporter

Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) likely will be a game-time decision for Thursday night's game in Baltimore, coach Liam Coen said Wednesday. Tuten, who is coming off the best game of his career (104 yards, a TD and a TD catch), did not practice at all this week. Tuten leads the Jaguars in rushing (492 yards). If he's unable to play, the Jaguars will likely start Chris Rodriguez Jr and behind him will be Ameer Abdullah and LeQuint Allen Jr.

Nov. 4: Shedeur Sanders could start with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol
By Eric Moody

Watson entered the concussion protocol Tuesday after reporting symptoms from a helmet-to-helmet hit in Sunday's loss to Pittsburgh. If he can't clear it in time for Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints, Sanders would likely start. He averaged just 11.9 fantasy points per game in seven starts last season, throwing seven touchdowns and nine interceptions. That's not encouraging for a Browns passing offense that ranks 22nd in passing yards per game this season.

Quinshon Judkins led the Browns' backfield with 13 touches against Pittsburgh but scored only 6.9 fantasy points, as Dylan Sampson led the backfield in snaps and routes, finishing with 12.9 fantasy points. The matchup against the Saints is much better for Judkins, as they allowed the most fantasy points per game to running backs. I'd still view him as a low end RB2, but his workload could be reduced if Cleveland falls behind again. Sampson is worth holding in most leagues and has flex appeal in deeper formats.

KC Concepcion was among Cleveland's leaders in routes against Pittsburgh but saw only four targets and scored 6.7 fantasy points. Harold Fannin Jr. (12 targets) and Denzel Boston (11) both saw more targets last week. I'd have a hard time trusting Concepcion or Boston in most fantasy lineups if Sanders starts..

Fannin is the one Cleveland pass catcher I'd feel comfortable starting. He caught 10 passes for 154 yards last week and has drawn at least nine targets in consecutive games. He's best viewed as a low-end TE1 if Sanders starts.

Nov. 4: Darnold out, Milton to start, Brissett traded
By Adam Rank

Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Sunday's game because of a quad injury he sustained on Monday night. Darnold has not been placed on IR, so you're going to need to either release him (which is fine in single-quarterback leagues) or put him on the bench in superflex leagues. The latter makes the most sense for Drew Lock as a replacement option.

However, if you're in traditional leagues with a realistic waiver wire, my first option would be to look at Malik Willis, who has averaged more than 20 points in Week 7 and 8. Willis has an advantageous matchup against the Detroit Lions, who have been very generous to opposing quarterbacks -- particularly mobile quarterbacks. The Lions are dead last against the pass (24.7 fantasy points per game).

Joe Milton was named the Philadelphia Eagles' starter, replacing Tanner McKee. Milton doesn't offer much upside for those of you in redraft leagues that start one QB. Don't even bother to make a waiver claim. However, if you're like me and you play in a superflex dynasty league, now we're talking. In fact, I'm in two such leagues. In one, I already had him rostered. In the other, I put in a huge claim for him. Mostly because my two starting quarterbacks are Jaxson Dart (IR) and Justin Herbert. And yes, I'm coming to the stunning realization Milton might be my best starting quarterback if I do end up getting him. I kid, but just barely.

The thing that intrigues me about Milton is his rushing ability. He had over 400 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns at Tennessee. And he's shown some flashes of mobility during very limited time as an NFL quarterback. I'm getting dangerously close to starting him in redraft, but will just opt for the dynasty play here.

In additional quarterback news, ESPN is reporting that QB Jacoby Brissett is expected to be traded to the Baltimore Ravens over the weekend. While Brissett is a streamable option moving forward, this is great news for Ravens WR Zay Flowers. There is concern about Flowers this Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but he will move back to his low-end WR1/WR2 status if the deal for Brissett is completed.

Nov. 3: Bears roster full of must-starts, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back into mix

By Michael F. Florio

The Chicago Bears offense continued rolling on the road Monday night against the defending Super Bowl champs. D'Andre Swift was the star of the show, turning 30 opportunities into 79 yards and three touchdowns. He finished with 27.9 fantasy points and surely dragged many fantasy teams from the jaws of defeat.

Luther Burden III stayed hot, racking up seven catches on nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. He finished with 18.6 fantasy points and has averaged 19.9 fantasy points per game since Caleb Williams returned in Week 6. He has emerged as the Bears' top pass catcher and is a weekly start.

Tight end Colston Loveland also saw nine targets, catching seven for 65 yards (and losing a fumble) to finish with 11.5 fantasy points. He has averaged 16.6 fantasy points per game since Williams returned. He should be started each week.

More takeaways from Monday

Williams played extremely well, even if it did not translate to the biggest fantasy game. He is the first QB to throw for over 200 yards against the Seattle Seahawks defense this season. He finished with 13.98 fantasy points. That is more about the matchup though. Williams should be started weekly.
Rome Odunze saw six targets, catching four for 87 yards, good for 12.7 fantasy points, his second-highest mark in a game this season. It's great to see Odunze produce, but he remains the third target in this Bears passing game. That makes him a low-floor, high-upside flex option.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to be the Seahawks' offense. He saw 11 targets, catching six for 118 yards and a touchdown. He deserves to be in the MVP conversation and should be viewed as the best WR in fantasy football. He has one game with less than 22.8 fantasy points this season (12.6 in Week 4). He has 52% of his team's receiving yards. No other player even has 40%.
Both Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returned from injury in Week 9. Price led the way, playing 48% of snaps and logging 10 carries and four targets. He finished with 37 total yards and 5.7 fantasy points. Charbonnet played 36% of snap and saw six carries and four targets. He went for 29 yards and finished with 5.9 fantasy points. The Seahawks have a better matchup next week against the Arizona Cardinals, but splitting the usage leaves both running backs purely as flex options.
Sam Darnold continued to struggle, but he ended up having a solid fantasy night, as Seattle was trailing and having to throw. He finished with 188 passing yards, two touchdowns, one interception and 17.52 fantasy points. Darnold has nine interceptions in his last six games. Still, he is a streaming option next week against the Cardinals, who are tied for the most passing touchdowns allowed in the league (18).

Nov. 2: How the move to Minshew impacts the Cardinals

By Michael F. Florio

The Arizona Cardinals named Gardner Minshew II as their starting quarterback on Monday for the Week 9 game in Seattle against the Seahawks.

Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett on Sunday against Dallas and threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns in a comeback win against the Cowboys, but faces a much tougher task next week against Seattle.

The biggest question is what this means for the Cardinals' pass catchers, but here's how I expect the switch at QB to impact all positions on offense.

While a QB change always adds some volatility, Trey McBride remains a must-start tight end. McBride is a must start regardless of who the QB is, but Minshew's tendency to target tight ends at a high rate keeps him as an elite option. In both 2023 and 2024, Minshew threw to tight ends 12% of the time, which is actually a higher rate than Brissett this season (10%).
Due to volume, Michael Wilson will remain in play in most matchups. However, next week against Seattle is a week to get him out of your starting lineup. The Cardinals next three weeks are tough matchups for Wilson. Outside of Wilson, fantasy managers should avoid the rest of the Cardinals receivers for the time being.
The running backs could see a bump in targets as well, as Minshew has always targeted running backs at a high rate. His career average is 17%, while Brissett is at 13% this season.
As for Minshew himself, fantasy managers should stay away with the next three weeks being the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs. For Week 9, some more favorable streaming options are Kyler Murray (or potentially Carson Wentz), Malik Willis, Sam Darnold and C.J. Stroud.

It is worth noting that since 2021, there have been 12 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who went on to make another start at some point in that given season; that group averaged 6.7 fewer fantasy points as starters (shout out to Tristan H. Cockcroft for the stat!).

Nov. 2: Notebook for Week 8

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills

Derrick Henry's playing time has declined over the past two weeks, falling below 50% of snaps against the Bills. On Sunday, he rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, marking his third straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill played on more snaps and ran more routes compared to Henry's nine, benefiting from Baltimore playing from behind. With Lamar Jackson headed for IR due to a thumb injury, the Ravens could struggle to sustain drives and generate red zone opportunities, making Henry's fantasy outlook even more concerning going forward.
Dalton Kincaid played through a chest injury against the Ravens and delivered his second-best fantasy performance (18.6 fantasy points) of the season, catching four out of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown. Kincaid continues to share playing time with Dawson Knox, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He ran 23 routes (compared to Knox's 17) and his targets per route remain high despite a slight decline in snaps. Kincaid has now stockpiled 14 targets over his past two games and remains a solid TE1 heading into Week 9 against the Vikings.

Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals

Wan'Dale Robinson continues to be Tennessee's most reliable receiver. He led the Titans in both snaps and routes against the Bengals, catching six out of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown. He has now drawn at least six targets in four straight games and remains a flex option. Chimere Dike caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown while filling in for Carnell Tate, but his role could shrink after the Week 9 bye. TE Gunnar Helm had his best game of the season with five receptions for 76 yards on nine targets, despite playing on a season-low percentage of snaps. Daniel Bellinger's increased involvement makes Helm difficult to trust outside deeper leagues.
Chase Brown led Cincinnati's backfield in snaps, routes and touches against the Titans. Brown finished with 55 rushing yards on 12 carries and caught eight out of nine targets for 46 yards, scoring 16.1 fantasy points. He also ran more than twice as many routes as Samaje Perine, highlighting his significant role in the passing game. Perine finished with just five touches for 19 yards but remains involved in the red zone. Brown's workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 conversation heading into Week 9 against a Falcons defense that ranks among the top five in fantasy points per game allowed to running backs. Perine remains as merely an insurance back.
Mike Gesicki set a season-high in snaps against the Titans following injuries to Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson. He ran three times as many routes as Drew Sample, and caught four out of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown (17.6 fantasy points). Gesicki has now scored a touchdown in five straight games, but what's even more encouraging is his increased involvement on early downs and in two-TE sets. With All and Hudson out for the rest of the season, Gesicki's expanded role should continue. He's worth adding for fantasy managers needing help at tight end.
Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions

The Vikings used a three-man backfield against the Lions, with no running back playing more than 40% of snaps. Aaron Jones Sr. led the way, followed by DeeJay Dallas and Jordan Mason. Mason led the backfield with eight carries for 20 yards, while Jones had five carries for 22 yards and caught both of his targets for 18 yards. Dallas handled most of the third-down work but finished with just one touch. Jones and Mason remain difficult to trust as anything more than flex options until their roles become clearer. However, the Vikings face a Bills defense in Week 9 that has allowed the fourth-most RB fantasy points per game.
Jordan Addison has seen increased playing time in the slot over the last two games, giving him more opportunities in the Vikings passing game. Against the Lions, Addison led Minnesota receivers in snaps and caught three out of eight targets for 11.6 fantasy points. Justin Jefferson led the team with nine targets, while Jauan Jennings had just two. Addison's eight targets were a season high, which is encouraging for managers. The Vikings face the Bills and Packers over their next two games, both of whom rank among the top 10 in terms of the most WR fantasy points per game.

Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys

Tyler Allgeier took over Arizona's backfield against the Cowboys after Jeremiyah Love aggravated his ankle injury and Bam Knight suffered a concussion. Love opened the game as the primary back, with Knight taking over early-down work following his departure. Once Knight exited, Allgeier played every running back snap in the second half and overtime. He finished with 147 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding five receptions for 44 yards and another score for a season-high 36.1 fantasy points. Allgeier should be a priority waiver pickup with RB2 upside if Love and Knight miss Week 9 against the Seahawks. His performance could also earn him a larger role even when both return.
Arizona's receiving corps continues to battle injuries. Kendrick Bourne suffered an ankle injury, Reggie Virgil exited late, and Michael Wilson played through broken ribs. Trey McBride and Wilson dominated snaps and routes, with Wilson drawing a team-high 15 targets and finishing with 111 yards and a touchdown. McBride added seven receptions for 72 yards and a score. He's now caught at least seven passes in 10 straight games -- the third-longest streak in NFL history. Both remain must-start fantasy options as targets continue to be concentrated between them. Gardner Minshew II also replaced Jacoby Brissett and could start in Week 9.
The Cowboys rank seventh in passing attempts per game, creating plenty of opportunities for their receivers. George Pickens has dealt with shoulder and hamstring injuries over the last two weeks, leading to more frequent substitutions and increased playing time for Ryan Flournoy. When Pickens has rotated out, Flournoy has handled most of the available snaps in single-receiver sets and taken on additional work in two-WR formations. Flournoy has now drawn at least four targets and scored at least 12 fantasy points in four straight games. Monitor Pickens' practice participation this week. If he remains limited, Flournoy could be an intriguing sleeper against a vulnerable Colts defense in Week 9.

Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers

Dylan Sampson led the Browns backfield in snaps, routes run and fantasy points (12.9), largely because Cleveland was playing from behind. Quinshon Judkins still led the backfield with 13 touches, compared to only seven for Sampson. This is something fantasy managers will have to live with when rostering Judkins, whose workload is more favorable when the Browns are playing with a lead or keeping games competitive. Cleveland should have an easier time moving the ball against the Saints in Week 9, keeping Judkins in the volume-based RB2 conversation.
KC Concepcion was held to four targets and 6.7 fantasy points against the Steelers after finishing with 10 targets and a season-high 23.2 fantasy points against the Titans in Week 7. Despite leading Cleveland in routes run, Concepcion was out-targeted by both Harold Fannin Jr. (12) and Denzel Boston (11). The playing time is encouraging, but the inconsistent target volume makes Concepcion and Boston difficult to trust in fantasy lineups. Fannin has been the more reliable option, drawing at least nine targets and scoring at least 13 fantasy points in consecutive games. He remains a low-end TE1.

Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets

The Raiders made a surprising change in their backfield against the Jets, giving Mike Washington Jr. the start over Ashton Jeanty. Washington dominated early-down and goal-line work, finishing with 83 rushing yards on a career-high 25 carries after never having reached double-digit attempts in any previous game this season. Jeanty played on a season-low number of snaps, managing just 9 yards on two carries but catching three passes for 64 yards. Coach Klint Kubiak said the change wasn't disciplinary and expects both backs to remain involved. Washington should be a priority waiver pickup, while Jeanty's reduced workload makes him a riskier fantasy option.
Braelon Allen led the Jets' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (23), finishing with a season-high 23.3 fantasy points. Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game, despite practicing on a limited basis throughout the week. Allen remains a must-hold for fantasy managers regardless of whether Hall is traded or stays in New York. He's played well enough to maintain a significant role, either as the lead back or in a committee with Hall. The Jets also have one of the more favorable remaining schedules for running backs, particularly after their Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs, making Allen worth holding for the stretch run.
Adonai Mitchell had a breakout performance against the Raiders, catching seven of his nine targets for 27.2 fantasy points. Garrett Wilson led the Jets with 12 targets, finishing with 14.3. Omar Cooper Jr. wasn't targeted, despite playing more snaps than Mitchell. Cooper continues to get more opportunities in two-WR sets, although Mitchell ran more routes against the Raiders. Mitchell will be a target on waivers, but the competition for playing time makes both receivers difficult to trust consistently. Wilson remains the safest fantasy option in this receiving corps.

Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars

The Colts continued to lean on Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs against the Jaguars despite trade rumors surrounding both players. Taylor played on 79% of snaps before garbage time but finished with just 12 touches and 6.7 fantasy points. Downs led Indianapolis in routes and caught four out of five targets for 12.3 fantasy points, thanks to a receiving touchdown. His playing time increased as the Colts used more three-WR sets while playing from behind. Their fantasy outlooks could change considerably, depending on what happens before the trade deadline.
Tyler Warren returned after missing the past two games due to a groin injury and led the Colts' TE room in snaps, routes, targets (10) and fantasy points (5.8). He saw a slight dip in playing time against the Jaguars compared to the first five weeks of the season, as Will Mallory took some additional snaps in 11 personnel. Although Warren had his second-worst fantasy performance of the season, he could take on a larger role in the Colts offense if either Taylor or Downs is traded.

Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown against the Falcons, finishing with 21 fantasy points. Irving and Kenny Gainwell split snaps evenly after Irving played on 64% of snaps over the first seven weeks. Irving remained the primary early-down back with 27 carries, while Gainwell handled all the passing-down snaps and rushed for 140 yards on 25 attempts. Poor weather conditions led Tampa Bay to run the ball on 90% of its plays, so I wouldn't expect this kind of split every week. Irving remains a must-start, having scored at least 21 fantasy points in three of his last four games.
Kyle Pitts Sr. has seen a slight dip in playing time over the last two weeks as he continues to split snaps with Charlie Woerner and Nick Muse, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He's drawn at least five targets in four straight games and scored at least 13 fantasy points in three of them.

Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams

Kyren Williams led the Rams backfield in snaps, routes and touches (17), but Blake Corum led the way with 13.3 fantasy points. Corum finished with 11 touches and both backs scored rushing touchdowns. Corum averaged 6.6 yards per carry, compared to 3.3 for Williams. He has now scored at least 13 fantasy points in four straight games and handled at least 10 touches in three of them. The Rams continue to lean heavily on their running game, keeping both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant.
The Chargers continued their three-man backfield rotation against the Rams, with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell splitting early-down work while Kimani Vidal handled passing situations. Vidal led the backfield in snaps and routes run, while Mitchell and Hampton saw similar playing time. Hampton finished with 27 total yards on 11 touches, while Vidal had 30 yards on 10 touches and Mitchell added 23 yards on seven touches. The Chargers offense has been a disaster, ranking last in points, touchdowns and turnovers this season. Limited opportunities and a three-man rotation make this a backfield fantasy managers should continue to avoid.

Kansas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos

Jonah Coleman took control of the Broncos backfield against the Chiefs with RJ Harvey sidelined by a knee injury. Coleman led the Broncos backfield in snaps and routes and finished with 41 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding four receptions for 63 yards (20.4 fantasy points). J.K. Dobbins managed just 13 yards on seven carries. Coleman also handled goal-line work and most of the second-half snaps, making him a must-add and a solid RB2 heading into Week 9 against a Panthers defense that's allowed the second-most RB fantasy points per game.
It was frustrating for Kenneth Walker III's fantasy managers to see Emmett Johnson finish with six touches and 25.3 fantasy points, compared to Walker's 25 touches and 12.3 fantasy points. However, context is important. Johnson played on a season-low number of snaps against the Broncos, while Walker continues to dominate touches in Kansas City's backfield. Walker has handled at least 20 touches in seven out of eight games this season. Johnson remains one of the top insurance backs worth rostering, but Walker's consistent workload should keep fantasy managers confident in his outlook.

New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins

DeMario Douglas led Patriots pass catchers with 16.6 fantasy points while A.J. Brown was ruled out and Romeo Doubs remained on IR. Douglas tied for the second-most routes run despite ranking fourth in snaps among New England's pass catchers. However, he's played primarily in 11 personnel this season, which could make his weekly production inconsistent, despite the strong performance.
Ollie Gordon II remains the Dolphins' clear lead back, playing on more than 80% of offensive snaps for the second straight week. He rushed for 69 yards on 19 carries against the Patriots but failed to catch his only target, finishing with 6.9 fantasy points. Gordon handled a season-high share of early-down snaps despite Jaylen Wright being fully healthy, while Kaytron Allen didn't see any offensive snaps. Gordon has averaged nearly 18 touches over his last four games, keeping him in the RB2 conversation. However, he has caught just one pass during that stretch, making him heavily dependent on rushing production and touchdowns.

Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders

The Commanders adjusted their receiving rotation with Terry McLaurin on IR. Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams took over as Washington's primary outside receivers against the Eagles. Both played season-high shares of snaps and ran more routes than Stefon Diggs, who continued to work primarily from the slot. Burks caught three passes for 81 yards, while Williams led the team with seven targets, finishing with five receptions for 54 yards. Diggs caught three passes for 38 yards and a touchdown. Burks and Williams are worth adding in deeper leagues, while Diggs remains a TD-dependent flex option heading into a difficult Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Wemby makes MVP opening statement
Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022.

"It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often."

With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there."

After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third in MVP voting last season and is seeking to become the award's youngest winner since Derrick Rose in 2011.

Nov. 4

NBA Trade Lab updates: Porzingis is popular in mock deals
In the first weeks since the release of ESPN Analytics' new NBA Trade Lab, the player involved in the most fan-created trades is Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis, who's in the news because the franchise is withholding payments from him while he's away from the team.

With 38-year-old legend Stephen Curry still playing at an elite level, it makes sense that fans want to see the Warriors make a swing to bolster his supporting cast. Add to that how good rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked to start the season, and Warriors fans might be right to think their favorite team isn't that far away from contention in the West, especially considering the early-season injury problems for the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Porzingis' $20 million salary would be a key ingredient for the Warriors to match salary in a potential trade.

Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Porzingis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved:

Trade No. 1

Warriors get: A shot-blocking stretch big in Myles Turner who could be a great fit in their motion-heavy offense to replicate some of Porzingis' game.

Milwaukee Bucks get: Porzingis and a young promising player in Moses Moody, who could be more valuable for the Bucks' rebuild. Moody is recovering from a torn left patellar tendon he suffered in March.

Trade No. 2

Warriors get: Daniel Gafford, who can provide rim protection and elite play-finishing. He would bolster their center depth and better exploit defenses that are stretched thin out on the perimeter drawn to Curry's gravity.
Dallas Mavericks get: Porzingis and a first-round pick swap to help reset their timeline around 19-year-old centerpiece Cooper Flagg, by improving their assets in a potentially loaded 2028 draft.

Trade No. 3

Warriors get: Talented 6-foot-8 forward Trey Murphy III, who can defend, draw fouls and rain 3s from well beyond the arc. At 26 years old, he also has the potential to be paired alongside Lendeborg as the wing duo of the future in the post-Curry era.

New Orleans Pelicans get: Porzingis, a promising young player in Moody and two future first-round picks to cash in on Murphy's value. Doing this deal would also provide more on-ball opportunities for 2025 lottery picks Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen.

Have any more ideas on what move the Warriors should make? Build them in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer

How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court

Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis?

[Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago.

"It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out."

Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade.

What Edwards' injury means for Wolves

On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery.

Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule.

But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches
stories.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international soccer with Portugal after being benched by coach Jorge Jesus. It is far from the first high-profile row of his career.
stories.body:
Editor's note: This has been updated after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer on Nov. 5, 2026.

Was it always going to end like this? Cristiano Ronaldo -- Portugal's greatest-ever player, who led them to victory at the 2016 UEFA European Championship, and won the UEFA Champions League and the Ballon d'Or five times in a glittering club career -- has called time on his international career.

Ronaldo, 41, walked away from the national team's camp last month after a row with coach Jorge Jesus. The Portugal boss insisted there was "no issue," but admitted mistakes in his handling of Ronaldo's role in the 2-1 win over Norway in the UEFA Nations League on Sept. 27, when he was an unused substitute.

Despite it seeming as though the coach and his captain had patched things up, Ronaldo confirmed on Thursday that he has played his last game for Portugal. However, an acrimonious end to his international career -- during which he has scored a men's record 146 goals -- could hardly be described as a shock.

- Ronaldo's incredible Portugal career: Best moments, key stats

- Siuuuu! The story of Ronaldo's career at Portugal, Man Utd, Real Madrid

- Ronaldo goal tracker: Every step on the road to 1,000 career goals

Managing the transition when an aging superstar's performance level drops is never easy, and Ronaldo's role and impact -- positive and negative -- with Portugal had been debated for three successive major tournaments, in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

Throughout his 25-year career, Ronaldo has been involved in a series of headline-grabbing disagreements with managers, teammates and executives. With his latest drama seemingly resolved, here are some of the most high-profile previous examples.

Unhappy Ronaldo backs Blatter's insensitive "slavery" comparison (July 10, 2008)
Ronaldo's bid to leave Manchester United for Real Madrid that summer reached a new, histrionic high -- or low -- when Ronaldo echoed comments from then-FIFA president Sepp Blatter that keeping a player at a club against their will was comparable to "modern slavery." Ronaldo told Portugal's TV1: "It's true. I agree with what the president of FIFA said. I know what I want and what I would like. We have to see what happens. I do not know where I will begin next season." After five successful years at Old Trafford, Ronaldo was ready to move on, but United stood firm and the forward had to wait another season before his desired move to the Bernabéu was finally fulfilled.

Ronaldo subs himself off mid-game at Old Trafford (Dec. 6, 2008)
Ronaldo abruptly walked off the pitch -- and headed straight down the tunnel -- midway through Manchester United's 1-0 win over Sunderland at Old Trafford. The team were left playing with 10 men, as United's coaching staff rushed to organise an unexpected substitution. Manager Sir Alex Ferguson defended Ronaldo, saying he had received "a kick on the hip" and "there was no need for Cristiano to come to the bench" when he required immediate treatment, but it was clear that the player -- who had won his first Ballon d'Or earlier that week -- was increasingly willing to act out.

Derby withdrawal sparks bout of Ronaldo head-shaking (May 10, 2009)
Ronaldo's reaction to another substitution, this time in the heated atmosphere of a Manchester derby, was the latest sign of a growing estrangement between him and the club. He had put United ahead against City with an 18th-minute free kick -- the first goal of a 2-0 victory -- but when Ferguson opted to replace him with Paul Scholes on the hour, Ronaldo reacted furiously. He spent several minutes shaking his head in frustration on the bench in a very public, visible showing of discontent. That opening goal proved to be his last for the club for 12 years.

No celebrations for "sad" Ronaldo (Sept. 2, 2012)
Three years on from finally getting his desired move to Real Madrid, new signs of dissatisfaction emerged. Ronaldo had scored twice in a 3-0 LaLiga win over Granada, but was he happy? No, he wasn't. The lack of a goal celebration for either strike raised eyebrows, and his enigmatic postmatch comments set alarm bells ringing. "I'm sad because of a professional issue, and the club know it," Ronaldo revealed, mysteriously. "That's why I'm not celebrating my goals, because I'm not happy. The people here know why." The forward refused to elaborate, and an explanation for his ennui was never forthcoming. Ronaldo subsequently denied that money was the problem, but a bumper new contract that was eventually signed a year later might have helped.

Mourinho hits back at 'know-it-all' Ronaldo (June 5, 2013)
Ronaldo and manager José Mourinho were close when the two first worked together at Real Madrid, but -- in a developing trend -- their relationship was deteriorating by the end of the 2012-13 season, Mourinho's last at the Bernabéu. A dressing room bust-up after a Copa del Rey game with Valencia in January was the beginning of the end and by June, after dropping the forward for the last few games of the season, Mourinho was telling TV show Punto Pelota after leaving Los Blancos for a second spell at Chelsea that "Cristiano Ronaldo thinks he knows everything."

Ronaldo prefers Carlo to Rafa (Dec. 11, 2015)
Rafa Benítez was in charge at Real Madrid for only six months after replacing Carlo Ancelotti in June 2015 and getting sacked the next January, but there was still time for his relationship with Ronaldo to come under scrutiny. There was speculation that the player was unhappy with his manager's tactical approach, and Ronaldo's fulsome praise for predecessor Ancelotti -- calling him an "unbelievable person" and a "fantastic coach" (and, rather endearingly, a "big bear") whom he "wished to work with again" probably didn't help. Benítez insisted that he and the star were still "adapting to each other," but there wasn't time for that: A month later, Benítez was gone.

Ronaldo benched ahead of United move (Aug. 22, 2021)
Just a few days before the 2018 World Cup final (in which Portugal were not involved), Ronaldo's move to Juventus after nine years in Madrid was announced. But, after three years in Turin, Ronaldo was ready to move again. He was left out of the team for the Italian giants' Serie A opener for the 2021-22 season, a 2-2 draw at Udinese, after reportedly asking not to start the match. Juventus were insistent that the forward would stay, and Ronaldo himself had earlier branded reports linking him with a move back to Real Madrid as "disrespectful." However, just over a week later, he was on his way back to Manchester United on transfer deadline day having been heavily linked with joining rivals City.

Ronaldo is no fan of three at the back (Jan. 19, 2022)
If we've learned anything so far, it's that Ronaldo isn't keen on being substituted. Manchester United interim coach Ralf Rangnick found that out when looking to protect the team's 2-0 lead at Brentford by replacing Ronaldo with Harry Maguire and switching to a back three. Ronaldo wasn't a fan of the tactical change, throwing his coat to the ground as he departed, before Rangnick had to have a word. The reaction was "normal," Rangnick said, adding: "I said maybe when you're a head coach yourself you will hopefully make the same decision." The coach was proved right: United went on to win 3-1.

'Nonsense' reports of Maguire captaincy battle (Feb. 18, 2022)
A month later, Rangnick was called upon to dismiss claims of a rift between Ronaldo and defender Maguire as "absolute nonsense." The issue at stake was reportedly the United captaincy, with skipper Maguire feeling threatened by Ronaldo's outsized influence in the dressing room among younger players. Rangnick sought to quash that, saying, "I have never spoken with any player about a possible change of captaincy," and insisting Maguire would continue in his role until the end of the season.

Explosive interview forces Ronaldo's second Old Trafford exit (Nov. 13, 2022)
After a start to the season that saw Ronaldo's goals dry up and his first-team place rescinded by new manager Erik ten Hag, Ronaldo's clear frustration came to a head when on Oct. 21 when he refused to come on as a substitute against Tottenham Hotspur, walked off down the tunnel and left Old Trafford before the final whistle -- something he also did during a preseason friendly with Rayo Vallecano.

His departure from United was finally sealed by a no-holds-barred interview with Piers Morgan. Ronaldo criticised just about everybody at Old Trafford -- saying he "didn't respect" Ten Hag, felt "betrayed" by senior executives, had "never heard of" Rangnick before his arrival and "zero progress" had been made since his first stint at the club. If the comprehensive takedown was designed to make his own position at United untenable, then it was a success, with the club agreeing to a departure by mutual agreement.

Ronaldo axed by Portugal, family reacts angrily (Dec. 6, 2022)
Ronaldo was dropped by coach Fernando Santos for Portugal's World Cup round-of-16 tie against Switzerland, and his replacement, Gonçalo Ramos, more than justified the decision, scoring a hat trick in a 6-1 win. Santos claimed the selection was based on "strategy," rather than Ronaldo's angry reaction to being substituted in Portugal's final group game, although Santos had previously said of his captain's outburst: "I didn't like it."

The Portuguese football federation (FPF) was then moved to deny reports that things had escalated before their quarterfinal against Morocco. "The FPF clarifies that at no time did the captain of the national team, Cristiano Ronaldo, threaten to leave the national team at any stage," it said in a statement.

Unsurprisingly, Ronaldo's omission didn't go well with the extended Ronaldo family. "What a shame not to have been able to enjoy the best player in the world for 90 minutes," partner Georgina Rodríguez said in a post on Instagram, and sister Elma Aveiro added: "It's a shame to humiliate a man who has given so much."

Ronaldo storms out of Portugal camp (Sept. 30, 2026)
And so here we are, waiting for Ronaldo to expand on the reasons for his latest walkout.

At the time of writing, we know that his exit followed a lack of minutes against Norway on Sunday, and then coach Jesus giving his version of events in a news conference three days later. Ronaldo, according to his own statement, then held "a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation." He also felt the need to wish his teammates "good luck, without exception" in Thursday's Nations League game with Denmark.

The last four years have been relatively calm by Ronaldo standards, with the forward scoring lots of goals -- and winning a couple of trophies -- with Al Nassr in the Saudi Pro League, and benefitting from a national team coach, Roberto Martínez, who backed him persistently at two major tournaments, despite growing criticism.

Jesus worked with Ronaldo at Al Nassr, but on this week's evidence, their relationship appears much less comfortable. We'll find out soon enough if it signals the end of a 23-year international career.

Ronaldo calls time on Portugal career (Nov. 5,2026)
After Portugal's matches ended in the Nations League for the international window, Ronaldo released a statement about what happened behind the scenes between him and Portugal coach Jesus, and what his future holds with the team.

In his statement, he accused Jesus of breaking two promises. The first was that the coach told Ronaldo that he should be ready to play 30 minutes against Norway -- where Portugal won 2-1 in Oslo -- at lunchtime on the day of the match. Ronaldo ended up not playing.

The second was that Jesus had agreed to address the issue in the press conference on the day prior to their match against Denmark in Copenhagen, following private conversations between him and Ronaldo.

The points that were to be brought up in the news conference ranged from "wanting Cristiano on the national team" to admitting he "made a mistake in having someone of the stature of Pelé or [Diego] Maradona warm up and then not putting him into game."

Jesus later said in the conference that "every player knows the coach makes the decisions" and that Ronaldo told him he would abide by whatever choices he makes, adding that the "rules are the same for everyone."

After that, Ronaldo left the team camp, and Portugal ended up winning the next two matches without him in the squad. The statement continued by saying that he "apologizes to his national team teammates for having left the camp" and says that "the consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation."

He closed it by saying that he "promises to have one or more farewell matches" and that "he will be available, as I always have been until today, to compete and win for our national team." However, we now know that will not be the case.

Portugal's upcoming matches against Denmark and Wales to close out their Nations League group will be their first without their captain, top scorer and greatest-ever player.

stories.headline: WNBA Finals saw surge in attendance, record ratings
stories.summary: The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999, with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the seven-game series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999, with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive Game 7.

That game averaged 3.3 million viewers, making it the most-watched WNBA postseason game ever. It was up 128% from last season's clinching game between Las Vegas and Phoenix that the Aces won.

All seven games in the series were sold out, including Game 6, which was played at 12:30 p.m. ET.

The Finals capped the WNBA's most-watched postseason since its inaugural season in 1997, averaging 1.49 million viewers, up 27% from last year.
